interpretationPolicy: The mapped Witchery names and separately inspected pages/images contribute only the broad role, social behavior, posture, clothing category, material, and palette cues enumerated below. Every Warlockery anatomy, proportion, face, costume construction, accessory arrangement, negative space, model part, pivot, hierarchy, UV layout, texture pixel, and animation must be independently authored. No historic image or source asset was incorporated into the concept artwork.

vampireVariantContract.selection: Select masculine versus feminine deterministically from the entity UUID and reproduce the same selection on every extraction, reload, and client. Do not add a gameplay, NBT, or network field unless implementation discovers an existing appropriate visual-state seam that cannot satisfy stable UUID selection.

requiredSemanticParts: long face-framing and three-back-current kelp hair panels
visible forearms with pearl tide cuffs

requiredTests: prove both UUID-selected variants are reachable
prove the same UUID always selects the same variant without mutable gameplay state
prove the two dedicated texture locations are selected with their matching geometry
prove both texture atlases exist, have pinned dimensions, have recorded SHA-256 hashes, and have different hashes
prove variant-specific hair, collar or bodice, shoulder, cuff, veil, coat, and train visibility differs semantically within VampireModel
prove VampireModel never extends, wraps, or delegates geometry to a vanilla player model or shared Warlockery humanoid rig
vampireVariantContract.bloodThrallSeparation: BloodThrallModel remains a separate independently authored lean low-bound rig, atlas, UV layout, state extraction, and animation implementation. It must not scale, subclass, copy, or reuse VampireModel geometry, variant helpers, or textures.

lycanVillagerClothingRendererContract.currentEntityFact: LycanVillagerEntity extends Villager and already carries synchronized live VillagerData containing type, profession, and level.
lycanVillagerClothingRendererContract.requiredStateSeam: LycanVillagerModel.State must extend VillagerRenderState, or implement VillagerDataHolderRenderState while extracting entity.getVillagerData() into the render state.
lycanVillagerClothingRendererContract.requiredModelSeam: LycanVillagerModel must implement VillagerLikeModel<LycanVillagerModel.State>, retain independently authored wolf head, muzzle, ears, hands, feet, body, pivots, and animations, and expose profession/type clothing-compatible robe, jacket, hat, and level-badge UV islands plus a no-hat body layer.
lycanVillagerClothingRendererContract.requiredForgeLayer: The dedicated Forge Lycan Villager renderer must add the native VillagerProfessionLayer with path 'villager', compatible main and no-hat LycanVillagerModel layers, and live VillagerData extraction.
vanillaCompositionSemantics: render villager biome/type texture from textures/entity/villager/type/<type>.png
render profession texture and profession headwear from textures/entity/villager/profession/<profession>.png
honor VillagerMetadataSection.Hat NONE, PARTIAL, and FULL visibility rules
preserve farmer, cartographer, armorer, nitwit, biome/type, and level identity dynamically instead of authoring one fixed outfit
requiredTests: source-check the native VillagerProfessionLayer(path='villager') seam and LycanVillagerModel VillagerLikeModel contract
prove render-state extraction retains the entity's VillagerData type, profession, and level

prove cartographer remains visibly cartographer and hat metadata selects the no-hat layer correctly
prove there is no custom fixed profession outfit texture, indigo vest, static apron, or static profession selection
